Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.

Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Question: Which electoral district is Albignac associated with?
Document 1: As the sun dipped behind the rolling hills of Corrèze, casting a warm orange glow over the sleepy commune of Albignac, the villagers began to stir. It was a crisp autumn evening, and the air was alive with the scent of ripe grapes and woodsmoke. In the town square, a group of locals gathered around the ancient fountain, their faces aglow with the soft light of lanterns. Among them was Pierre Dupont, the village mayor, a stout man with a bushy mustache and a kind heart. He stood tall, his eyes twinkling with a hint of mischief, as he addressed the crowd. "Mes amis, the time has come to discuss the upcoming elections. Our beloved canton of Bapaume needs our voices to be heard, and I propose we send a delegation to represent Albignac's interests." The villagers murmured in agreement, their faces nodding in unison. It was no secret that Albignac's fate was deeply entwined with that of the canton of Bapaume. For generations, the commune had relied on the canton's support for its agricultural endeavors, and in return, Albignac's rich soil and skilled farmers had contributed to the canton's prosperity. As the meeting drew to a close, a young woman named Sophie slipped out of the crowd, her dark hair tied back in a loose braid. She made her way to the local bakery, where the aroma of freshly baked bread wafted out into the night air. Inside, she found the baker, Monsieur LaFleur, kneading dough with a look of intense concentration. "Sophie, my dear, what brings you here so late?" he asked, his flour-dusted hands pausing mid-air. "I came to ask about the canton's electoral district, Monsieur LaFleur," Sophie replied, her eyes sparkling with curiosity. "Pierre mentioned it in the meeting, but I'm not entirely sure what it means for us." Monsieur LaFleur's face creased into a thoughtful expression. "Ah, yes. The canton of Bapaume. Well, you see, Sophie, our commune is part of that electoral district. It means we have a say in the canton's decisions, and they, in turn, provide us with resources and support. It's a partnership that's served us well over the years."

Albignac is a commune located in the Corrèze department in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region of France. As a part of the French administrative system, Albignac is associated with the electoral district of the canton of Midi Corrézien. Evidence of Association

The association between Albignac and the canton of Midi Corrézien is supported by multiple credible sources. Furthermore, the French Ministry of the Interior's website lists Albignac as one of the communes in the canton of Midi Corrézien. [3] The Ministry of the Interior is responsible for overseeing the country's administrative divisions and electoral districts. In addition, various online mapping and geographic information systems, such as GeoHive and MapQuest, also show Albignac as part of the canton of Midi Corrézien. [4][5]

Conclusion

The evidence from multiple credible sources, including the INSEE, the Corrèze department's official website, the French Ministry of the Interior, and online mapping and geographic information systems, confirms that Albignac is associated with the electoral district of the canton of Midi Corrézien.
